# Power ups need to be larger — Intake Brief (AH-0MTG5MGPZ00986B4)

## Problem statement

Power-up drops are too small and visually inconspicuous, making them difficult to pick up during play. Players need drops to be twice as large with a clearly visible glowing bubble (circle) around each drop so pickups are immediately legible and more forgiving to collect.

## Users

- **Players** — struggle to collect small drops under fire; benefit from larger, high-contrast pickups that are easier to see and overlap.
- **Gym testers / developers** — need the sizing and bubble semantics defined once so every drop type renders consistently.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want power-up drops to be twice as large so I can collect them without pixel-perfect positioning.
- As a **player**, I want each drop surrounded by a glowing bubble/circle so I can spot it instantly against the black background and busy bullet patterns.
- As a **developer**, I want the size and bubble defined as tunable constants / shared visuals so GymPowerUps and GymWeapons both render the same way.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Drops are twice as large:** `POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE` and `WEAPON_DROP_SIZE` (canonical in `src/core/constants.ts`) are doubled from 16 → 32 px (or equivalent scale factor of 2×). All drop types use the new size, including non-combat (P5, P8, P9) and weapon (Spread, Dual, Rapid, Reset). Mirrored/re-exported constants (`src/powerups/PowerUp.ts`, gym scenes) remain consistent.
- [ ] **AC2 — Glowing bubble around every drop:** Each on-field drop renders a glowing circle/bubble surrounding its icon. The bubble is code-drawn (Phaser Graphics, no external assets), in the neon style (e.g., per-type aura colour or white with outer glow), centred at the drop position and scaled with the lifecycle scale (grow/hold/shrink). GymPowerUps renders the bubble (currently no drop graphics — must add) and GymWeapons adds the bubble alongside its existing weapon icon graphics.
- [ ] **AC3 — Collection remains correct and more forgiving:** Overlap collection (`_overlapsShip` in both gym scenes) uses the new size (`DROP_SIZE * currentScale + hull`) so the effective pickup radius is doubled at full scale. Drops are still gated by the >3% collection threshold; collecting plays the existing per-type audio.
- [ ] **AC4 — Lifecycle visuals scale correctly:** Bubble + icon scale 0 → 1 → 0 with the `PowerUp` lifecycle (`advance()`) so the growing/shrinking animation remains smooth and framerate-independent; fully despawned drops remove their graphics.
- [ ] **AC5 — Testing/validation:** Existing drop/collection/magnet/weapon suites still pass with the new size (overlap thresholds updated where they hard-code 16). At least one new or updated test asserts: (a) the doubled size constant, (b) the bubble graphics are created per drop and scaled with lifecycle, (c) overlap distance at full scale is doubled. Manual visual check in GymPowerUps and GymWeapons shows the bubble clearly.
- [ ] **AC6 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Code-first, no external art assets — bubble is drawn with Phaser Graphics / lineStyle primitives (neon vector aesthetic, GDD §7.1).
- Engine: Phaser v4 + TypeScript; web + Windows binary compatible (GDD §6.3).
- Tunable size lives in `src/core/constants.ts` (single source of truth); scenes and `src/powerups/` re-export or import from there.
- Do not change effect semantics, lifetimes, spawn cadence, or magnet math — only size and visuals.

## Existing state

- `src/core/constants.ts` defines `POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE = 16` and `WEAPON_DROP_SIZE = POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE`; `HUD.ts` draws HUD icons at size 8 (not in scope).
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` draws per-type power-up icons (`drawPowerUpIcon`) and weapon icons (`drawWeaponIcon`) at the caller-supplied size; no bubble is drawn today.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts` tracks `ActiveDrop { powerUp, x, y }` with no per-drop Graphics — drops have no on-screen visuals beyond lifecycle bookkeeping. Overlap uses `POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE * currentScale + hull`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` creates a `Graphics` per weapon drop, draws the weapon icon at `WEAPON_DROP_SIZE`, and scales it with `currentScale`; no bubble.
- `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` / `effects.ts` / `spawner.ts` are size-agnostic (lifecycle is time-based, not px-based).

## Desired change

1. Double the canonical drop size constant (16 → 32) in `src/core/constants.ts`; ensure `WEAPON_DROP_SIZE` follows and re-exports stay consistent.
2. Add a glowing bubble visual for every on-field drop:
   - Introduce or extend a shared helper (e.g., in `src/powerups/icons.ts` or a small visuals helper) that draws a neon circle/bubble around the icon.
   - GymPowerUps: add per-drop Graphics (icon + bubble) with lifecycle-scaled `setScale(currentScale)` and proper `destroy()` on despawn/collect.
   - GymWeapons: extend existing per-drop Graphics to also draw the bubble around the weapon icon, still scaled with lifecycle.
3. Update overlap helpers to use the new size (already parametric — verify) and update any tests that hard-code 16 or near-field distances.
4. Verify visually in both gyms and via tests.

## Key Files

- `src/core/constants.ts` — Double `POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE` (16 → 32); `WEAPON_DROP_SIZE` follows; single source of truth.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — Add bubble-drawing helper (e.g., `drawPowerUpBubble` / `drawDropWithBubble`) or extend existing icon draw to include glowing circle; neon style, per-type colour.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts` — Add per-drop Graphics for icon + bubble; scale with `powerUp.currentScale`; create/destroy lifecycle; overlap uses new size.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — Extend per-drop Graphics to include bubble alongside weapon icon; keep lifecycle scaling and spawn/despawn audio.
- `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` — Update constant comment/reference if needed (re-exports `POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE` mirror).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts`, `src/powerups/PowerUp.test.ts` — Update or add assertions for doubled size, bubble presence, and scaled overlap.

## Related work

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 Power-Ups, §6.4 architecture, §7.1 neon aesthetic — authoritative spec for drop appearance.
- Work item "Power-up core lifecycle + tunable constants" (AH-0MTCNZPHN003C5E1) — introduced `POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE` and lifecycle constants.
- Work item "Power-up catalogue + effects (P5, P8, P9)" (AH-0MTCNZX16007ECPS) — non-combat catalogue.
- Work item "Create gym scene for power-ups with spawning, collection, and standalone HUD" (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) — GymPowerUps scene (currently no drop graphics).
- Work item "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene" (AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR) — GymWeapons scene (has drop graphics).
- Work item "Create gym scene for power-ups with spawning, collection, and standalone HUD" children: spawner, lifecycle, HUD — context for constants layout.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** keep to sizing + bubble only; do not add new power-up types, particle systems, screen-shake, magnet visual changes, or HUD resizing in this item. Record extras as linked work items.
- **Visual tuning is subjective:** bubble radius, stroke width, glow alpha, and per-type colour may need playtest iteration. Mitigation: expose bubble constants alongside `DROP_SIZE` in `src/core/constants.ts` (e.g., `POWER_UP_BUBBLE_RADIUS_FACTOR`, `BUBBLE_GLOW_ALPHA`) so feel is tunable without code churn; tests assert geometry, not exact colour.
- **Assumption — both drop families in scope:** "Power ups need to be larger" is read as applying to all on-field drops (P5/P8/P9 and Spread/Dual/Rapid/Reset). If operator intended only non-combat drops, note as a follow-up — but default to all for consistency.
- **Assumption — bubble is visual only:** the bubble does not add extra collection radius beyond the doubled drop size; overlap stays `DROP_SIZE * scale + hull`. If a larger aura-based pickup is desired, file a follow-up.
- **Assumption — HUD unchanged:** HUD icons remain at 8 px in `src/ui/HUD.ts`; only field drops grow. No GDD §4.4 count/ID changes needed.
- **GymPowerUps graphics gap:** adding Graphics per drop is behaviour-neutral for logic tests (harness must support `add.graphics`) but may require test updates; verify `src/test/gameHarness.ts` and GymPowerUps tests.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should both families of drops (non-combat P5/P8/P9 and weapon Spread/Dual/Rapid/Reset) be doubled and get the bubble, or only the non-combat drops shown in GymPowerUps?" — Answer: **Assumed both** — brief scopes both `POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE` and `WEAPON_DROP_SIZE` (identical constant) and both gym scenes. Rationale: title says "Power ups" generically and constants are shared; a split would be noted as a follow-up. Source: no operator reply requested; inference from repo search (keyword `power` hits both families, constants shared at 16 px). Traceability: `src/core/constants.ts:63/98`.
- Q2: "Is the bubble purely visual, or should its radius also count for collection (aura pickup)?" — Answer: **Assumed visual only** — collection stays `DROP_SIZE * scale + hull` with the doubled size; bubble does not add extra radius. Rationale: original request says "a bubble around them (a glowing circle)" — visual phrasing, not "larger pickup aura". Source: intake draft assumption; no operator reply solicited (seed context sufficient). Traceability: `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts:_overlapsShip`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts:_overlapsShip`.
- Q3: "Any preference for bubble styling (per-type neon colour vs white glow, thickness, pulsing)?" — Answer: **Assumed neon-style outline circle with subtle outer glow, centred at drop, radius ~1.3–1.5× drop size, scaled with lifecycle, per-type aura colour matching `ICON_COLORS` / weapon colours.** Rationale: matches GDD §7.1 neon vector aesthetic and existing `ICON_COLORS` mapping in `src/powerups/icons.ts`; keeps the implementation code-first with no assets. Source: repo inspection of `src/powerups/icons.ts` and GDD §7.1. Traceability: `src/powerups/icons.ts:ICON_COLORS`.

Potentially related docs

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 Power-Ups (drop semantics), §6.4 powerups/ layout, §7.1 neon aesthetic (bubble styling constraint).
- `README.md` — Gym coverage / "Run the game" context if visuals are noted.
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` — harness for gym scene tests; GymPowerUps graphics addition must remain testable.

Potentially related work items

- AH-0MTCNZPHN003C5E1 Power-up core lifecycle + tunable constants (completed)
- AH-0MTCNZX16007ECPS Power-up catalogue + effects (P5, P8, P9) (completed)
- AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT Create gym scene for power-ups with spawning, collection, and standalone HUD (completed)
- AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene (completed)
- AH-0MTCNZPHN003C5E1 / AH-0MTCPL9NA0025ZUI surrounding spawner lifecycle items (completed)

# Intake Brief — [Refactor] Remove unused export THRUSTER_HUM_DETUNE_SPREAD_CENTS (AH-0MTP19DG100472CV)

## Problem statement
`src/audio/effects.ts` exports `THRUSTER_HUM_DETUNE_SPREAD_CENTS = 12` but nothing imports it. The hum now uses private drift constants (`THRUSTER_HUM_DETUNE_DRIFT_MAX_CENTS` / `_STEP_CENTS`) for organic random-walk detune; the exported spread is dead compat cruft that inflates the public surface and confuses readers with two overlapping detune concepts.

## Users
- **Developers maintaining `src/audio/effects.ts`** — want a minimal, accurate public API without dead exports to mis-import.
- **Future thruster-audio contributors** — avoid confusion between the legacy spread constant and the active drift system.

### Example user stories
- As a developer, I can read `src/audio/effects.ts` exports and see only actively used constants, so I don't reintroduce the legacy detune path.
- As a reviewer, I can trust that `grep` for an export finds its consumers or confirms it is intentionally removed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1 — Export removed:** `src/audio/effects.ts` no longer exports `THRUSTER_HUM_DETUNE_SPREAD_CENTS` (no `export const THRUSTER_HUM_DETUNE_SPREAD_CENTS` remains); the REFACTOR marker comment for this item is removed.
- [ ] **AC2 — No consumer missed:** `grep -rn THRUSTER_HUM_DETUNE_SPREAD_CENTS` across the repo (excluding `.worklog` worktrees) finds zero hits at merge time; no `src/**` or test file imports the symbol.
- [ ] **AC3 — No behaviour change:** Thruster hum still uses `THRUSTER_HUM_DETUNE_DRIFT_MAX_CENTS` / `THRUSTER_HUM_DETUNE_DRIFT_STEP_CENTS` (private consts) for detune drift; audible behaviour and lifecycle unchanged.
- [ ] **AC4 — Verification:** `npm run typecheck` (`npx tsc --noEmit`) and `npm test` (`vitest run`) pass locally.
- [ ] **AC5 — Docs/comments intact:** Adjacent export comments and the detune-spread compat comment are removed/updated so no stale reference remains.
- [ ] **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- [ ] **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints
- Do not change runtime thruster hum behaviour; this is a pure export-surface cleanup.
- The package is `private: true` (`package.json` v0.1.2) with no published external API contract — removal is safe if repo-global search is clean.
- Keep change surgical: touch only `src/audio/effects.ts` (plus the injected REFACTOR comment block).

## Existing state
- `src/audio/effects.ts:59` — `export const THRUSTER_HUM_DETUNE_SPREAD_CENTS = 12;` with comment `// Detune spread retained for compat (jet roar no longer uses harsh detune).` (now outdated).
- Active detune system is private: `const THRUSTER_HUM_DETUNE_DRIFT_MAX_CENTS = 8` and `const THRUSTER_HUM_DETUNE_DRIFT_STEP_CENTS = 2`, used in `ensureThrusterHum` and `updateThrusterSound` for random-walk drift.
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` does not import or assert `THRUSTER_HUM_DETUNE_SPREAD_CENTS`.
- Repo-global grep (excluding `.worklog` worktrees) returns only the definition line; no consumer.

## Desired change
- Remove `export const THRUSTER_HUM_DETUNE_SPREAD_CENTS = 12;` and its `// Detune spread retained for compat …` comment from `src/audio/effects.ts`.
- Remove the `<!-- REFACTOR-AH-0MTP19DG100472CV … -->` marker comment block injected at the top of `src/audio/effects.ts` once the cleanup ships.
- Verify with `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm test`.

## Key Files
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Remove the unused export (line 59) and its compat comment; delete the REFACTOR marker block (lines 9–13) on completion.
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — No change expected; confirms no test depends on the removed export (verify before merge).

## Related work
- AH-0MTP19JIB004ORC0 — [Refactor] Deduplicate thruster teardown in effects.ts (sibling refactor on same file; low risk of merge conflict — coordinate if both touch the header comment block).
- AH-0MTK9JP37003MJQ4 — Thruster hum: add tonal randomization and noise/grit (introduced the drift constants that replaced the spread).
- AH-0MTK9ZSOX009SB1K — Thruster hum: jet-engine roar — remove buzzy sawtooth (context for why harsh detune / spread was dropped).
- AH-0MTHF3SA7009A4LK — Implement thruster hum in effects.ts (original hum implementation).
- AH-0MTHF3ST7007VLUL — Update GDD §7.3 and code comments for thruster hum (GDD §7.3 describes hum as 60 Hz triangle + 35 Hz sine + band-pass noise; does not reference DETUNE_SPREAD — no doc update needed).

## Risks & assumptions
- **Risk:** External out-of-repo consumer imports the constant. **Mitigation:** `package.json` is `private: true`; no published API. Repo-global grep is the verification gate (AC2).
- **Risk:** Merge conflict with sibling teardown refactor touching the same header. **Mitigation:** Both are header/comment-only vs export-line changes; rebase cleanly, keep each marker removal isolated.
- **Assumption:** No documentation (GDD, README, wiki) references `THRUSTER_HUM_DETUNE_SPREAD_CENTS` — verified via grep; no update needed beyond code comment removal.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Do not expand to broader thruster-audio refactoring (e.g., deduplicating teardown) — that is tracked separately in AH-0MTP19JIB004ORC0; file any extra opportunities as linked work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers
- No interview questions were required. The seed context and repo-global search (`grep -rn THRUSTER_HUM_DETUNE_SPREAD_CENTS`) were sufficient to confirm the export is unused and the replacement drift constants are private. Verification was done against `src/audio/effects.ts`, `src/audio/effects.test.ts`, and `docs/Game Design Document.md` (no reference to DETUNE_SPREAD).
- If the producer knows of an out-of-repo consumer that depends on this export, flag it before implementation — the fallback is to demote to a non-exported internal const rather than delete outright.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTK9ZSOX009SB1K** – Thruster hum: jet-engine roar — remove buzzy sawtooth (completed)
- **AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q** – Create E1 Scout gym scene (completed)
- **AH-0MTBOOV0J008QCVM** – Documentation: GDD §7.2 + code comments for direction-neutral ship (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance (+148 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+138 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: ac1, ac4, active, add, api (+104 more)
